findings: The public finite-mass couplers and link springs carry stored energy, and the stated outer calorimeter measures thermostat heat rather than spring work into the main coordinate. With signed heat into the apparatus, Q_i=W_i+Delta(E_link_i+E_coupler_i).

The full eight-dimensional stationary Langevin state is used by both controls. Calibration mode correlations are identical and stationary mean outer heat equals mean spring power, so calibration does not expose the finite-window distinction.

The oracle combines exact stationary Gaussian work variance, endpoint energy variance and work–endpoint cross covariance. Its mixed terms have the correct ordering under time-lagged stationary covariance.
The independent reference evolves E[Q], E[Q*z*zT] and E[Q^2] from the direct Ito outer-heat stochastic differential. Its same-bath noise cross term and gamma*T/M Ito drift are correct.
Finite masses remove overdamped work ambiguity. The stationary joint preparation, bath index and unreduced accumulated variance are explicitly specified.
